suspect:thomas_crale: Thomas Crale leaned on the gate with his arms folded. His boots were clean but the cuffs of his trousers carried dried clay.
event:altered_path: The boundary path had been moved twelve feet to the south. The old line was still visible as a depression in the grass.
motive:boundary_fraud: The altered boundary added four acres to the Crale holding. The extra land covered the shortfall on his debt to the bank.
suspect:amos_webb: Amos Webb farmed the adjoining field and had quarrelled with Fell over access. His dog was loose in the orchard that evening.
suspect:ruth_crale: Ruth Crale served tea to the inspector and said nothing about the boundary. Her hands were steady but her eyes did not leave the window.
suspect:mr_hadley: Mr Hadley was the parish surveyor and had measured the boundary the previous year. His original notes differ from the filed record.
suspect:ned_garvey: Ned Garvey drank with Jonas Fell at the village inn on the afternoon of the death. He said Fell mentioned a discrepancy in the maps.
suspect:eliza_banks: Eliza Banks kept the parish records and filed the land deeds. She had placed a rival bid on the orchard six months earlier.
suspect:constable_price: Constable Price was first to reach the body at dawn. He noted the position of the stakes before anyone else arrived.
location:crale_orchard: The orchard covers three acres on a south-facing slope above the river. The oldest trees are bare and the grass is long between the rows.
location:boundary_wall: The boundary wall runs along the western edge of the orchard. One section of stone has been rebuilt with fresh mortar.
location:farm_lane: The farm lane connects the orchard gate to the village road. Wheel ruts and boot prints cross in both directions.
location:parish_office: The parish office holds land records going back to 1804. The filing cabinet nearest the window holds current boundary maps.
location:crale_farmhouse: The farmhouse sits fifty yards from the orchard gate. A light burned in the kitchen window until after midnight.
location:village_inn: The village inn serves as courthouse and public house. Jonas Fell signed his last letter there at four in the afternoon.
location:tool_shed: The tool shed stands behind the farmhouse wall. An iron pry bar hangs from a nail beside the door.
location:river_crossing: The river crossing lies below the orchard at the bottom of the slope. The stepping stones are slippery after rain.
object:survey_stakes: Three wooden survey stakes stand at the new boundary line. The paint is fresh and the wood has not yet weathered.
object:boundary_map: The boundary map in the parish office shows the Crale holding twelve feet wider than the 1921 survey. The ink colour differs at the western edge.
object:iron_pry_bar: An iron pry bar was found in the tool shed with soil on its end. The bar matches the marks on the displaced boundary stone.
object:parish_ledger: The parish ledger records all boundary amendments by date and witness. The latest entry has a single witness signature.
object:debt_notice: A bank notice addressed to Thomas Crale was found in the farmhouse bureau. The outstanding sum matches the value of four acres.
object:fell_notebook: Jonas Fell's field notebook was found beside the body with three pages torn out. The remaining pages show measurements that contradict the filed map.
object:moved_stone: A boundary stone has been levered from its original position and re-seated. The base shows a ring of fresh mortar.
object:boot_scraping: Boot scrapings on the orchard gate post match a size eleven sole. Amos Webb wears size eleven.
object:rope_fragment: A length of rope was found tied to the boundary stone. The fibres match the rope stock in Crale's tool shed.
object:land_deed: The land deed for the Crale orchard was refiled at the parish office four months ago. The new filing adds four acres to the western boundary.
object:lamp_glass: A broken lamp glass was found at the base of the boundary wall. The oil had soaked into the grass beneath it.
object:soil_sample: Soil from the boundary stone base does not match the surrounding ground. The clay is consistent with the riverbank below the orchard.
object:chain_measure: Fell's surveyor chain was found fully extended between two stakes. The measurement reads twelve feet longer than the filed record.
emotion:guarded_calm: He answered each question about the boundary with the same flat tone. His pipe remained unlit in his hand.
emotion:quick_anger: Webb stood up from his chair when the boundary was mentioned. He sat down again without being asked.
emotion:false_sympathy: Crale spoke of Fell as a thorough man and a loss to the county. He did not mention that Fell had written to the bank.
emotion:stiff_silence: Hadley looked at the filed map and said nothing for twelve seconds. He then asked whether the original survey still existed.
emotion:nervous_laughter: She laughed once when asked about the refiled deed. The sound stopped abruptly and she reached for her tea.
emotion:flat_denial: He said he arrived at dawn and found the body exactly as it lay. His account did not change across three tellings.
modifier:stake_repositioned: The western survey stakes stand twelve feet south of the depression left by the original markers. The soil around each stake is loose.
modifier:fresh_mortar: The mortar joining the re-seated boundary stone is a lighter colour than the rest of the wall. It has not yet fully cured.
modifier:mud_on_handle: The pry bar handle carries dried mud matching the orchard topsoil. The grip pattern is consistent with a bare right hand.
modifier:lamp_extinguished: The lamp was found with its glass broken and the wick cold. Oil pooled beneath it suggests it fell from a height.
modifier:gate_unlocked: The orchard gate was found unlatched at dawn. Crale stated he locked it at six the previous evening.
modifier:ink_alteration: The boundary line on the parish map is drawn in two inks. The western section is darker and applied with a finer nib.
modifier:soil_disturbed: The soil around the boundary stone base is loose and mixed with clay. The clay does not occur naturally at that elevation.
modifier:rope_knotted: The rope around the boundary stone is tied in a bowline. Crale served in the merchant navy where the bowline is standard.
modifier:bruise_pattern: The bruise on Fell's temple is consistent with the flat end of a pry bar. The angle suggests a blow from the right.
modifier:boot_print: Boot prints near the body match a size eleven sole with a worn left heel. Webb and Garvey both wear size eleven.
action:stone_levered: The boundary stone was levered from its bed using an iron bar. The leverage marks match the tool shed pry bar.
action:map_redrawn: The parish map was amended by hand with a darker ink. The amendment was not countersigned by a second surveyor.
action:path_cleared: The original boundary path was cleared of its markers and the grass combed flat. Only the soil depression remains.
action:ledger_amended: The parish ledger entry for the Crale boundary shows a correction in different ink. The witness column has one signature instead of two.
action:drink_offered: Ned Garvey bought Fell a pint at four and they spoke for an hour. Garvey said Fell seemed worried but did not say about what.
action:gate_opened: The orchard gate was unlatched from inside using the drop bolt. The bolt is stiff and requires force to lift.
action:deed_filed: The refiled deed was submitted by Eliza Banks on behalf of Crale. The original deed has not been returned.
action:notebook_removed: Three pages were torn from Fell's notebook after the measurements were taken. The tear marks suggest haste.
action:rope_cut: The rope was cut six inches from the knot with a sharp blade. The cut is clean and made in a single stroke.
time:dusk_hour: Fell was last seen alive at the boundary wall shortly before dusk. The light was failing and he carried a lamp.
time:afternoon_survey: Fell began his survey of the Crale boundary at two in the afternoon. He worked alone with his chain and notebook.
time:morning_discovery: Constable Price found the body at first light beside the boundary stone. The dew had settled and the grass was undisturbed around the path.
time:filing_deadline: The bank required proof of acreage by the end of the month. Without the extra four acres, the debt exceeded the collateral.
time:last_light: The sun set at half past five and the orchard was dark within the hour. No lamp was seen from the farm lane after six.
motive:land_debt: Crale owed the bank more than the farm was worth at its current size. The four extra acres brought the collateral above the debt.
motive:acreage_claim: The amended boundary gave Crale a strip of rich bottomland along the river. The strip had been common grazing for thirty years.
motive:survey_suppression: Fell's survey would have revealed the boundary had been moved. His report was due at the parish office the following morning.
motive:family_name: The Crale family had held the orchard for three generations. Losing it to the bank would end a name in the parish register.
motive:rival_bid: Eliza Banks had offered to buy the orchard at auction six months earlier. If Crale defaulted, she was positioned to acquire it.
witness:postman_ridge: The postman saw Fell walking toward the orchard at two with his chain over his shoulder. He did not see anyone else on the lane.
witness:milk_boy: The milk boy passed the orchard gate at half past five in the morning. The gate was open and he saw no lamp or figure.
witness:vicar: The vicar spoke with Fell at the inn before the survey. Fell said he expected the measurements would not match the filed record.
witness:inn_landlord: The inn landlord served Fell and Garvey at four. He said Fell left at five with his bag and did not return.
witness:ploughman: The ploughman worked the field below the river crossing until dark. He heard nothing from the orchard above.
event:jonas_fell_discovered: Jonas Fell was found beside the western boundary stone at dawn. His notebook lay open and his lamp glass was broken.
event:boundary_inspection: The boundary inspection was ordered by the parish council after a complaint from Amos Webb. Fell was appointed to conduct it.
